clue.text: A sailor lacking refinement said to get some military training

indicators.note: said tells us the phrase before it is spoken, and the entry is what we hear

parts.note: a sailor is a SALT, so 'a sailor' is A SALT; lacking refinement means COARSE

explanation.surface: An uncouth seaman is sent off for a spot of army drill.
explanation.walkthrough: A SALT COARSE spoken out loud gives the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An army obstacle circuit of walls, nets and ditches is a standard piece of soldiers' physical training.

clue.text: They're used by Turks fighting racism — it's wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are set out incorrectly, so they get rearranged

explanation.surface: A protest against racism, declaring it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turks fighting racism' reads as a campaign, but the definition stops at 'fighting'; RACISM and ITS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Curved Oriental swords were the classic weapons of Ottoman soldiers in battle.

clue.text: Mostly hostile states

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Most countries are unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like a noun for countries; it is the verb meaning declares. AVERSE loses its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare firmly, so the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Had close relationships with ladies I mistreated

indicators.note: mistreated signals the letters are handled badly and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cad confesses to affairs with women he treated badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to work in close contact and cooperation; the word also hints at a love affair.

clue.text: Naval cutter in dock joined by young woman

indicators.note: joined by puts the second piece straight after the first

parts.note: to dock a tail is to cut it

explanation.surface: A navy boat in harbour is met by a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naval cutter' looks like a small ship, but it is a sailor's sword; 'dock' is the verb, not the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A short broad sword favoured by sailors is literally a seaman's cutting weapon.

clue.text: Deceptive and unorthodox kind of service

definitions.meaning: in tennis or cricket bowling, a delivery made with the hand below the shoulder

explanation.surface: A tricky, unconventional tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Underarm play is the old-fashioned delivery, while the word also means sneaky and dishonest.

clue.text: Fight in nocturnal creature's home over nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the next

parts.note: a sett is a badger's burrow

explanation.surface: A scrap breaks out in a badger's den, over nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A badger is a night animal native to Britain, and its burrow is a sett.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief brawl or argument is a hyphenated noun for a scrap.

clue.text: Without a vote, is candid and fresh, unusually so

indicators.note: unusually says the letters come in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone deprived of a vote is unusually frank and cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: IS, CANDID and FRESH together are rearranged; 'and' and 'so' just join.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stripped of voting rights is to be deprived of the franchise.

clue.text: Disputed editors cutting things like this, occurring four times here

indicators.note: cutting puts the editors into the middle of the other word

parts.note: this puzzle is a crossword, so things like it are crosswords

explanation.surface: Editors argue about cutting puzzles, with something happening four times in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occurring four times here' points to the theme: four pairs of sword names cross in this grid, as SCIMITARS does CUTLASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who have clashed in argument are said to have fought each other, figuratively with blades.

clue.text: Wanderer repeatedly without home

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps round the other

explanation.surface: A homeless rover keeps moving on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller who moves from place to place is a roaming person.

clue.text: Over time does, for example, hold back

indicators.note: over means covering, so one word goes round the other

explanation.surface: Over time, someone does a thing such as holding back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb; it is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage or prevent someone from acting is to restrain them.

clue.text: Contrasts seen in fine art works

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Contrasts are visible in good paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sense of fencing swords is part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing that sets off another by contrast is called that, and the word is also a fencing blade.

clue.text: Silly dons spar about nothing — they're used to cut and thrust

definitions.text: they're used to cut and thrust

indicators.note: about places the following item inside the rearranged letters
silly suggests the letters are jumbled in a foolish way

explanation.surface: Foolish academics fence over nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: DONS SPAR rearranged is wrapped round O.
explanation.definitionFit: These were light swords designed both to slash and to stab.

clue.text: Frightened a learner with a gun, say

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
carrying a weapon such as a gun is being armed

explanation.surface: A learner was scared when holding a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alarmed is being worried or scared.

clue.text: Statement of policy, if not same, must be changed

indicators.note: the letters must be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A party platform must alter if it is no longer identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party publishes its declared aims before an election.

clue.text: Some split hairs to modernise this Asian language

definitions.text: Some split hairs to modernise this Asian language

parts.words: Some split hairs to modernise this Asian language
parts.note: part of the words 'split hairs' spells the present name of the language, which replaced the older name being clued

explanation.surface: Pedants quibble about updating an Asian language's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in 'spliT HAIrs' is THAI, the modern name for the language of Siam; the answer is the old name that THAI modernises.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of Thailand was called after Siam, the country's former name.

clue.text: Legendary brand's former quality, as proclaimed?

parts.note: EX means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: as proclaimed means we hear the word spoken rather than read it

explanation.surface: A famous trademark's past quality, as advertised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand' looks like a trademark, but an old sense is a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's sword is legendary, and brand is a poetic word for a sword.

clue.text: In which, people gamble and endlessly cash in? Not so

indicators.note: endlessly applies to each of the four words in turn, so every one loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Gamblers hope to win money there, but mostly do not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks as if it governs only 'cash', but it trims all four words after it; the question mark marks the wry comment on gamblers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambling houses are the places where people bet.

clue.text: Yield small volume you aim, ultimately, to store in reserve

indicators.note: to store in means the following pieces are kept inside the reserve

parts.note: a sub is a substitute player
CC is cubic centimetres, a small volume

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter

explanation.surface: Give in, with a small amount you want kept in store.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in or surrender is to submit, a synonym.

clue.text: Leads astray spies holding foreign nobleman

indicators.note: holding means one word contains the other

explanation.surface: Secret agents capture a foreign aristocrat and lead him astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spies' looks like a noun; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone into wrongdoing or sex is to entice them.

clue.text: As sign, dangerous creature rendered harmless?

indicators.note: a creature with its sting removed is harmless, so its tail letter is removed

explanation.surface: A deadly animal made safe, appearing as a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: The creature loses its last letter, its tail being where the sting is.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve zodiac signs.

clue.text: Thereby extracted from clips of actors

indicators.note: extracted from says the letters are taken from within the words

explanation.surface: Film snippets taken from performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase meaning by that very fact.

clue.text: Fish under stone, kind of blue or grey

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the fish below the stone

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight

explanation.surface: A fish lying beneath a stone is bluish-grey.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel blue and steel grey are colour names taken from the metal.

clue.text: Article from Spanish city that was historically used in fighting

definitions.text: that was historically used in fighting

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so the article leaves

parts.note: Bilbao is a city in Spain's Basque Country

explanation.surface: An object from a Spanish city was once used in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like an object, but it is the word A.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of sword made in Bilbao was a historical fighting weapon.

clue.text: Almost swallowed part of apple or pear, say

definitions.text: part of apple or pear, say

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to swallow a story is to believe it, to buy it

explanation.surface: Nearly gulped down part of an apple or pear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallowed' is to accept a lie; 'apple or pear' are the trees, not fruits.
explanation.definitionFit: A main limb of a fruit tree is a branch.

clue.text: Fencers use them to ensure most of enclosure gets put back

indicators.note: put back means the letters are turned round

parts.note: to see to it is to ensure

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Fencers use them to ensure most of their enclosure is returned.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE and PE together are read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sport swords with stiff blades used in fencing.

clue.text: Fruit tree in a French garden area not explored in depth

indicators.note: in places the fruit tree inside the other pieces

parts.note: a plum is a fruit tree

explanation.surface: A fruit tree in a French garden plot is unexplored.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to measure depth, so unmeasured depths are unsounded.

clue.text: Cares about large and diverse brood — they are biologically related

indicators.note: about means the worries go round the other letters
diverse suggests the letters are varied

explanation.surface: A parent worries about a big, varied family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cares' looks like a noun of concern and is the worries word; 'and' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Male siblings share parents and blood, hence a genetic kinship.
